name: Singapore
summary: An island city-state at the tip of the Malay Peninsula. After separating from Malaysia in 1965 it became one of the world’s richest countries and busiest ports.

location.value: An island city-state off the southern tip of the Malay Peninsula, about one degree north of the equator.

terrain.value: A main island and over 60 smaller islands; land reclamation has greatly enlarged its area since the 1960s.

climate.value: Tropical rainforest climate with no distinct seasons, high humidity and abundant rain; usually 23–32 °C.

resources.value: Lacks natural resources and a hinterland; its favourable position made it a trading hub.

disasters.value: Haze from bush fires in neighbouring Indonesia, often from July to October.

population.value: About 6.1 million (mid-2025), of whom about 3.7 million are citizens.

urbanisation.value: A city-state; 78.7% of resident households live in public housing flats built by the Housing and Development Board (HDB).

disease.value: The SARS outbreak (2002–2004) and the COVID-19 pandemic.

migration.value: About 44% of the workforce is non-Singaporean, including about 224,500 foreign domestic workers (2013).

economicBase.value: Financial services, manufacturing and oil refining; one of the world’s busiest ports.

tradeRoutes.value: On the Strait of Malacca; one of the busiest ports.

wealth.value: The highest PPP-adjusted GDP per person in the world.

moneyAndTax.value: The Singapore dollar; low tax rates on personal income.

inequality.value: Moderate; high incomes but large gaps between top earners and low-wage workers.
inequality.source: Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore (2009)

governmentType.value: A parliamentary republic; constitutionally multi-party, but dominated by the People’s Action Party since 1959.

keyRulers.value: Lee Kuan Yew (prime minister 1959–1990). Goh Chok Tong. Lee Hsien Loong. Lawrence Wong (since 2024).

succession.value: Regular elections; the People’s Action Party (PAP) has kept continuous dominance since 1959.

institutions.value: A strong, well-paid civil service, strict anti-corruption laws and the Housing Development Board.
institutions.source: Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore (2009)

stability.value: Race riots in 1964 and 1969; since then political stability has been credited to the “Singapore model”.

eliteConflict.value: Low; leadership changes have been planned within the ruling party.
eliteConflict.source: Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore (2009)

armyAndTech.value: Conscription for able-bodied men at age 18.

majorWars.value: Indonesia’s Konfrontasi against Malaysia included the MacDonald House bombing in Singapore (1965).

territoryChange.value: Expelled from Malaysia and independent on 9 August 1965; land reclamation keeps adding land.

alliancesRivals.value: Founding member of ASEAN (1967); close ties with the US and China.

inventions.value: NEWater (high-grade reclaimed water, launched 2003) and large-scale land reclamation.
inventions.source: ADB, "Harry Seah: making the unthinkable drinkable" (checked 10 Nov 2026); Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore (2009)

scienceEducation.value: Pupils score at the top of international tests; strong universities (NUS, NTU).
scienceEducation.source: Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore (2009)

openness.value: A free, business-friendly economy and a major trade, finance and shipping hub.

communicationTransport.value: MRT and LRT trains, buses and taxis; Changi Airport (opened 1981) links about 300 cities.

religion.value: Buddhism 30.9%, Christianity 17.1%, Islam 15.0%, Taoism and folk beliefs, and Hinduism (2020).

languageWriting.value: Four official languages: English, Malay (national language), Mandarin and Tamil.

artsArchitecture.value: Landmarks include the Merlion, the Esplanade, Marina Bay Sands and Gardens by the Bay.

socialStructure.value: Multiracial: about 74% Chinese, 13.5% Malay and 9% Indian (2020).

sharedIdentity.value: Multi-racialism is written into the constitution, and meritocracy is heavily emphasised.

dailyLife.value: Most live in HDB flats; hawker centres; Hainanese chicken rice is the national dish.

neighbours.value: Malaysia (across the Johor Strait) and Indonesia.

ideasReligions.value: Multiculturalism and religious harmony; Buddhism, Christianity, Islam, Taoism and Hinduism.
ideasReligions.source: Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore (2009)

colonisation.value: Raffles set up a British post in 1819.

riseSignals.value: Independence in 1965 after expulsion from Malaysia; rapid growth made it one of the Four Asian Tigers.

peakPeriod.value: Still exists; growth averaged about 6% a year between 1965 and 1995.

declineSignals.value: Not applicable: still exists. Challenges include an ageing population and high costs of living.
declineSignals.source: Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore (2009)

outcome.value: Continues today as the Republic of Singapore.
